  set client_remote "[IP::client_addr]:[TCP::client_port]"
  set client_local  "[IP::local_addr clientside]:[TCP::local_port clientside]"
  set server_local  "[IP::local_addr]:[TCP::local_port]"

text:
TCP::remote_port
Description
Returns the remote TCP port/service number of a TCP connection. This
command is equivalent to the BIG-IP 4.X variable
remote_port
. When
used in a clientside context, this command returns the client-side TCP
source port, and is equivalent to the
TCP::client_port
command. When used in
a serverside context, this command returns the server-side TCP
destination port, and is equivalent to the
TCP::server_port
command.
Syntax
TCP
::
remote_port
[
clientside
|
serverside
]
TCP::remote_port
Returns the remote TCP port/service number of the current context’s
TCP connection.
TCP::remote_port
clientside
Returns the remote TCP port/service number of the client-side TCP
connection.
TCP::remote_port
serverside
Returns the remote TCP port/service number of the server-side TCP
connection.
Examples
when
HTTP_REQUEST
{
if

HTTP

uri
]
contains
"/secure/"
}
{
pool
ssl_pool
}

{

http_pool
}
}

{

TCP
::
remote_port
]
!=
443
}

SSL
::

}
}

log

}

Version Specific Notes
Prior to BIG-IP v9.3.0, using this command
with a “Performance (Layer 4)” (aka. “fastL4”) profile would produce
an error; this issue is tracked as CR58658. The workaround is to use
the
eval
command to force execution of the command. For example:
when
CLIENT_ACCEPTED
{
set
cmd
"set remote_port [TCP::remote_port]"
eval
$cmd
log
local0.
"Remote port is: $remote_port"
}
